The group of Prof. Dr. Eva Nowack, Institute of Microbial Cell Biology at Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf is looking forPostdoc (m/f/d) in Endosymbiosis ResearchJob-ID: J000000668Working hours: Full timeLocation: DüsseldorfStart date: 01.01.2027Limited until: 31.12.2028Apply till: 21.10.2026Payment group: EGr. 13 TV-LOrganization: MathematischNaturwissenschaftliche FakultätJob Category: science / research / teach To support our ongoing research, we are seeking a highly motivated Postdoctoral Researcher to join our team. Our group is an enthusiastic and collaborative team of cell and evolutionary biologists investigating the evolutionary transition from bacterial endosymbionts to eukaryotic organelles. We seek to understand, at the mechanistic level, how protists interact with permanent bacterial endosymbionts and how these associations evolve toward organellogenesis. To address these questions, we combine state-of-the-art omics approaches with detailed molecular biological and protein biochemical experimentation. As model systems, we have established the photosynthetic amoeba Paulinella chromatophora and the symbiont-harboring trypanosomatid Angomonas deanei and related species in the laboratory. Our work has provided exciting insights into organellogenesis and enabled us to develop novel tools for dissecting the molecular and cellular biology of host-symbiont interactions (see e.g., Morales et al. (2023) Curr Biol. doi: 10.1016/j.cub.2022.11.020.; Sørensen et al. (2024) FEBS J. doi: 10.1111/febs.17356; Maurya et al. (2025) Science Adv. doi: 10.1126/sciadv.adp8518; Klimenko et al. (2025) Plant Phys. doi: 10.1093/plphys/kiaf504; Hammond et al. (2026) Nat Commun. doi: 10.1038/s41467-026-70084-0.). The successful candidate will contribute to a current project at the heart of our research program, with the opportunity to shape the project in part according to their scientific interests, expertise, and strengths. The position will also involve a limited amount of undergraduate teaching in German [4 contact hours (Semesterwochenstunden) per week], providing an opportunity to contribute to the training of the next generation of biologists.A PhD in biology, biochemistry or a related areaAn excellent academic track recordResearch experience in microbiology or cell biology, genetic engineering, and advanced microscopy techniquesExperience with organelle biology, symbioses or protistology is a plusA strong motivation in experimental work, literature search and scientific writingReadiness to work independently and as a team player in an interdisciplinary, international teamFluency (oral and written) in English and GermanProactive character, creativity, communication and presentation skills, excellent organization and analytical skillsThe position is initially limited for a period of 2 years with the possibility of extension. It is a qualification position in the sense of the Act of Academic Fixed-Term Contract (Wissenschaftszeitvertragsgesetz - WissZeitVG), which is to promote the scientific qualification of the employee. The pay scale grouping will be 13 TV-L.Our BenefitsCompany pension grant; Good transport connection; Free parking; Flexitime; Working from home; Union rates; Part-time possible; Payment of capitalforming benefitsHeinrich Heine University upholds the principle of "Excellence through Diversity". jobs.employer_name: INM - Leibniz-Institut für Neue Materialien gGmbH
jobs.description: IntroductionINM is an internationally leading centre for interdisciplinary research on (bio)hybrid materials, and their exploitation in materials-based solutions for a sustainable world with increasing digitalization and medical needs. Our research integrates materials chemistry, biological processes, physical analysis, and process engineering. We aim for leadership in the fields of opto-interactive, electro-integrative and bio-intelligent material systems. In these areas, we actively seize opportunities to transfer our scientific results into materials-driven innovation.The INM research group, Bioprogrammable Materials, is looking for an enthusiastic Post-Doctoral Researcher with experience in microbial biotechnology and adaptive laboratory evolution (ALE). We combine synthetic biology, microbial engineering and sustainable materials research to develop innovative solutions for industrial and environmental challenges. We are seeking to fill a 2-year funded Post-Doctoral Researcher position as part of an Industrially-aligned European project developing sustainable biobased coatings. Neuronal exocytosis is a highly regulated process that enables the rapid release of neurotransmitters from synaptic vesicles. Central to this process is the controlled assembly of SNARE protein complexes, which drive membrane fusion and are regulated by a network of associated proteins. The PhD project will investigate the structural and molecular mechanisms underlying SNARE complex assembly and function in membrane-like environments. A particular focus will be placed on the development and characterization of membrane-mimetic systems, including lipid nanodiscs and synthetic copolymers, to study SNARE complexes and their regulatory proteins under increasingly native-like conditions. Cryo-electron microscopy will be combined with complementary biochemical and biophysical approaches to characterize these systems at the molecular level.The project offers the opportunity to work in an interdisciplinary structural biology environment at Forschungszentrum Jülich, with access to expertise in cryo-EM, NMR spectroscopy and X-ray crystallography. Cryo-EM studies will be conducted at the state-of-the-art facilities of the Ernst Ruska-Centre (ER-C) at Forschungszentrum Jülich. The expertise in NMR spectroscopy and macromolecular crystallography at IBI-7 offers further opportunities for complementary structural and biophysical characterization. This combination of methods will enable the candidate to address biological questions from different structural perspectives and to develop a broad expertise in modern structural biology. We are looking for a highly motivated candidate with:A Master’s degree in biochemistry, molecular biology, structural biology, or a related fieldStrong practical experience in protein biochemistry, including recombinant protein expression and purificationPrevious hands-on experience with cryo-electron microscopy and/or cryo-EM sample preparationInterest in membrane proteins, protein-protein interactions and structural biologyAbility to work independently as well as in an interdisciplinary research teamGood communication skills in English

jobs.description: Overview:Fairtrade is the most recognized and trusted sustainability label, working to make trade fairer for people and planet.For more than three decades, Fairtrade has been making an impact on the way trade works. We believe that every farmer and worker should have access to a better way of doing business, and a better way of living. Fairtrade International is an independent non-profit organisation representing more than two million small-scale farmers and workers worldwide. It owns the FAIRTRADE Mark, a registered trademark that appears on more than 37,000 products. Steward and drive the development, maintenance, and continuous improvement of the Theory of Change and MEL framework for several of the Fairer Futures Programmes, working in close collaboration with Producer Networks and Global Product Teams. Steward the KPI and activity/output indicator set for both programmes, including maintaining metadata and monitoring data quality. Work with PN MEL staff, Global Product Teams, and where needed external consultants to ensure systematic consolidation of existing programme data and the design and implementation of regular data collection processes. Coordinate with the Information & Knowledge team on data cleaning, analysis, and visualisation.- Stakeholder Engagement and Project MEL Alignment. Serve as Fairtrade International's primary MEL contact for the product-expert colleagues in Producer Networks and Global Product Teams, providing technical MEL guidance, supporting capacity on data collection and reporting, and ensuring programme MEL requirements are understood and operationalised across the system. Facilitate learning processes within programmes, identifying evidence-based insights and working with Global Product Teams and PNs to support programme adaptation where warranted. Ensure programme MEL evidence and KPI data are appropriately integrated into the overall strategy MEL cycle in close coordination with the designated strategy MEL lead within the Impact Management team.- Programme Evaluation.
